subject: Admin activity evidence: TTL, scoped extracts, redaction and export options
messages:
From: Lucas Grant <lucas.grant@acme-audits.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>; Compliance Team <compliance@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Admin activity evidence request — scope and TTL rationale

Hi Marissa,

We're kicking off the SOC 2 readiness work for Acme Health and need a clear, granular statement of what you log for admin activity plus the export/hand-off options. Specifically we need answers to: 

- Which admin action types are recorded (console sign-in, role changes, API key rotation, config changes, model pinning, user provisioning/deprovisioning, billing permission changes, etc.)?
- Per-event metadata: timestamp (including timezone), actor id, IP, session id, target resource, before/after where applicable.
- Retention policy per event type and rationale for TTLs (why 90d vs 365d etc); any tiering for legal hold or subscriptions.
- Redaction strategy for PII and protected fields in exports.
- Export formats supported (JSONL, Parquet, CSV), manifest/attribution, signed checksums, and delivery channels (SFTP, signed HTTPS bundle, cloud-share with encryption).
- Proof-of-export / chain-of-custody options (signed manifest, KMS-protected envelope, HMACs).

Also please confirm whether timezone normalization (UTC) is applied in exported timestamps and whether exported user identifiers are hashed/opaque for external delivery.

If you can provide a sample 100-row extract and a manifest with checksums for our review that would be ideal.

Thanks — we need this for our initial evidence mapping by end of next week.

Regards,
Lucas
Lucas Grant
Senior Auditor, Acme Audits

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Grant <lucas.grant@acme-audits.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>; Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity evidence request — scope and TTL rationale

Lucas — thanks for the clear checklist. High level answers below; Kimberly will follow with policy specifics and export mechanics. For timelines, we can produce a 100-row sample CSV + signed manifest within 48 hours and a full attested export within 5 business days assuming SFTP creds.

Quick summary: 
- Logged action classes: console auth events, role & permission changes, API key lifecycle (create/rotate/revoke), model deploys/rollbacks, config edits (route changes, routing policies), dataset access requests (admin-granted), and billing permission changes.
- Per-event metadata: UTC timestamp, internal user id (hashed on external export), email (internal only), source IP, session id, resource path, delta payload (before/after where available).
- Retention: default 365 days for admin events; high-privilege or legal-hold items retained 7 years or until release. We have a 90-day hot retention on high-frequency writes to improve query latency for live investigations — archived thereafter.
- Redaction: PII fields are redacted at export time by a field-level rule engine; salted HMAC is applied to user identifiers if the export target is external.
- Export options: JSONL (complete), CSV (columnar excerpt), Parquet (optimized bulk) — each export includes a manifest with SHA256 checksums and an MD5 quick-sum. Delivery: SFTP (preferred), HTTPS pre-signed object (timebound), or encrypted cloud-share (customer KMS).
- Proof-of-export: we can provide a signed manifest (PKI), KMS-wrapped envelope, and an HMAC over the manifest. Audit-trail of the export job (who triggered, job id, start/end time) is logged and included in the bundle.

I attached a compact manifest as a stub and will follow with a policy excerpt from compliance.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0148

Attachments: admin_activity_manifest_20260623.tar.gz (application/gzip)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Grant <lucas.grant@acme-audits.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>; Security <security@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity evidence request — scope and TTL rationale

Hi Lucas,

Adding the compliance perspective and concrete policy language you can use in your mapping. Apologies for the concise format — I wanted to give you actionable text for your SIG/SOC2 matrix.

Retention & TTL specifics (policy excerpt):
- Admin Event Category A (privileged access changes, role grants/revokes, API key revocations): retained 7 years for enterprise customers by default; 365 days for self-serve tenants unless legal hold requested.
- Admin Event Category B (config edits, route changes, model pin/unpin): retained 365 days with 90-day hot cache window and cold archive thereafter.
- Admin Event Category C (auth failures, console sign-ins, session tokens): retained 90 days for routine security monitoring; 365 days if correlated with an incident.

Export and redaction rules:
- Export jobs run in a sandboxed ETL process. Field-level redaction list is applied using deterministic rules; any field marked PII is replaced with "[REDACTED]" and an HMAC token is issued to preserve referential integrity if required.
- Time normalization: all exported timestamps are in UTC; original local timezone is preserved in the event payload under event_metadata.local_ts for forensic reference (not included in external exports unless requested).

Deliverables we can provide: 
- 100-row CSV sample with header explanations (non-PII) — attached as export_sample_excerpt_20260623.csv stub.
- Full export bundle: JSONL + manifest.tar.gz with SHA256 checksums, GPG-signed manifest, and export job audit record (JSON job_run_*.json).

Chain of custody and attestations:
- We sign manifests with our infrastructure signing key; we can also KMS-wrap the archive key and provide the encrypted envelope. For higher assurance customers we offer notarized attestations via a DocuSign flow.

If Acme needs different TTLs for regulatory reasons, we can support a contractual carveout on Dedicated or Private deployments; hosted tenants have the defaults above.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention_policy_summary_20260623.pdf (application/pdf), export_sample_excerpt_20260623.csv (text/csv)

From: Lucas Grant <lucas.grant@acme-audits.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity evidence request — scope and TTL rationale

Thanks Marissa / Kim — this is very helpful. A few clarifying requests so we can close the evidence mapping: 

1) For the sample CSV, can you include the hashed user_id and a separate column with an HMAC token so we can validate referential integrity across exports?
2) Can you confirm the manifest signature algorithm and provide a public key or the signing cert?
3) We prefer SFTP delivery to our inbound host (see sftp link below). Please confirm whether uploads are passive SFTP (port 22) and whether we need to provide an SSH key.
4) For timezone normalization: confirmed UTC in exports is acceptable — just need a note that local_ts exists in the raw payload for forensic pulls.

If you can send the 100-row sample and the GPG-signed manifest today that will be great. Also please attach the export job_run record (who triggered, job id, start/end timestamps) — that is essential for audit.

Regards,
Lucas

SFTP: sftp://sftp.acme-audits.com/incoming/redwood_marissa/

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Grant <lucas.grant@acme-audits.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>; Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity evidence request — scope and TTL rationale

Lucas — attaching the 100-row sample and a compact manifest stub. Answers inline: 

1) Sample CSV: includes columns (event_ts_utc, hashed_user_id, hmac_token, event_type, source_ip, session_id, resource, delta_preview). Hashed IDs are salted per-customer; HMAC token column present for referential checks. (See attached export_sample_excerpt_20260623.csv)
2) Manifests: we use SHA256 checksums and sign manifests with our infra GPG key (RSA-4096). Public cert for verification: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C_sample_export_manifest (cert.pem). We can also provide the cert as part of the export bundle.
3) SFTP: uploads use standard SFTP (port 22), key-based auth preferred. Please upload your SSH public key to the inbound directory we shared and we'll map it to the job account.
4) job_run record: included in the full bundle; for the sample we've attached a condensed job_run snippet in the manifest. Full job_run audit will be in the attested bundle.

Next steps: I will schedule the full attested export (JSONL + manifest + job_run + signed envelope) for Tue 30 Jun 2026 pending receipt of your SSH key. If you want DocuSign attestation, please let me know and I'll send the flow.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments included: export_sample_excerpt_20260623.csv, admin_activity_manifest_20260623.tar.gz
